public_rationale: The October 2023 survey treats factual reliability as unresolved after reviewing methods including retrieval and further training. That supports Marcus's ordinary claim that general-purpose LLM factuality could not be assured. The finding does not mean that factuality improvements were absent or that guarantees for restricted tasks were impossible.
limitations: Support rests on a contemporary research synthesis, not an exhaustive proof of nonexistence.
The result depends on reading the claim as about general-purpose use.
No numerical reliability threshold was supplied.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is no way to guarantee that large language models reliably stick to facts.

statement.excerpt: We have no way of guaranteeing that large language models will reliably stick to facts, a point so thoroughly established by now I don’t think it needs a reference.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that no established method assured factual reliability across general-purpose, open-ended LLM use. This is not a claim that constrained applications cannot provide any guarantees.

criteria.support_condition: Contemporary research identifies general factual reliability as unresolved after considering available mitigation methods, with no established general assurance method found.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A method available by the post date provided a substantiated factual-reliability guarantee covering general-purpose, open-ended LLM answers.
